briefings.title: Academia Job Shortlist

scope.geography: United States; Cleveland/Ohio prioritized when a sufficiently strong match is available
focus: New Approach Methodologies and human-relevant technologies
Tissue engineering, microfabrication, and biomedical engineering
Translational gastrointestinal and inflammatory disease research
scope.selection_rule: Include only academic or academic-medical-center roles that are meaningfully aligned with the candidate's research trajectory; exclude generic postdocs and faculty searches with weak scientific overlap.

jobs.title: Associate Staff Scientist (Intestinal Organoids)
jobs.company_info: Cincinnati Children's is a major academic pediatric medical center. This role is associated with the CuSTOM Accelerator, a multidisciplinary environment spanning scientists, clinicians, surgeons, bioengineers, computational scientists, and entrepreneurs working on organoid-based translational research.

salary.note: Range surfaced in the current job listing; verify the final institutional range before applying.

jobs.job_description: Support intestinal-organoid research within a multidisciplinary academic translational environment. The role is unusually close to the candidate's current scientific identity because organoids are not merely an assay component; they are central to the position.
key_must_have_requirements: Relevant advanced scientific training appropriate for a staff-scientist-level intestinal-organoid role
Hands-on mammalian cell culture and organoid experience
Ability to work in a multidisciplinary academic research environment
Strong experimental execution, documentation, and communication
jobs.why_good_match: The candidate already works at the intersection of patient-derived intestinal organoids, gut-on-chip engineering, host-microbiome interactions, and translational disease modeling. This role would use the organoid expertise directly while preserving access to bioengineering and computational collaborators rather than forcing a narrow shift into a single technique.
specific_experience_to_highlight: Patient-derived intestinal organoid culture and epithelial differentiation
Crohn's disease and inflammatory intestinal models
Cross-disciplinary work with bioengineers and computational scientists
gaps_or_risks: The salary appears low relative to many PhD-level industry scientist roles
A staff scientist track may provide less independence than a postdoc designed around a future faculty transition
Confirm whether the role provides first-author publication ownership, grant-writing opportunities, and clear advancement criteria
resume_tailoring: Lead with patient-derived intestinal organoids and translational gastrointestinal disease models
Present gut-on-chip engineering as a differentiator that extends organoids into more physiologic systems
Include scRNA-seq and computational interpretation as evidence of end-to-end biological analysis
Emphasize independent troubleshooting and protocol development
jobs.immediate_action_now: Review the PI/program structure and publication expectations before applying. If there is a credible path to scientific ownership, this is one of the strongest Ohio-based academic fits and is worth contacting directly in addition to submitting the formal application.

jobs.title: Director, Research Core (Advanced Human-Relevant Technologies)
jobs.company_info: The University of Louisville is a public research university. This role leads a research core centered explicitly on advanced human-relevant technologies, making it unusually aligned with organ-on-chip, NAMs, complex in vitro systems, and translational model infrastructure.

salary.note: Range surfaced in the current listing.

jobs.job_description: Lead an academic research core focused on advanced human-relevant technologies. The position is more infrastructure- and leadership-oriented than a traditional postdoc and would likely involve technology strategy, platform operations, collaboration, and support for investigators using next-generation human model systems.
key_must_have_requirements: Substantial relevant research and/or research-core experience
Ability to manage complex research infrastructure and multidisciplinary collaborations
Strong scientific communication and organizational leadership
Experience relevant to advanced human-relevant model technologies
preferred_requirements: Organ-on-chip, microphysiological systems, organoids, or related NAM technology experience
Technology implementation, validation, and user training
Grant, program, or collaborative project development
jobs.why_good_match: Scientifically, the title and mission are almost a direct match to the candidate's organ-on-chip/NAM identity. The candidate also brings rare breadth across device engineering, wet lab biology, microfabrication, CFD, bioinformatics, and human disease modeling. The concern is not scientific relevance but whether the role expects substantially more formal management experience than a newly graduating PhD typically has.
specific_experience_to_highlight: Translational NAMs and human-relevant model development
Microfabrication and porous PDMS membrane technology
Cross-platform integration of organoids, microbiome, and omics
Mentoring, protocol development, invention work, and research coordination
gaps_or_risks: This is a leadership position and may require significant prior core-facility or personnel-management experience
The minimum experience language may effectively target a more senior candidate
Running a core can shift effort toward operations and service rather than first-author research and independent discovery
resume_tailoring: Frame prior work as platform building, validation, standardization, troubleshooting, and user-facing technology development
Highlight mentoring, lab operations, documentation, and cross-disciplinary coordination
Present the invention and fabrication work as evidence of technology leadership rather than isolated engineering projects
Explicitly connect organ-on-chip work to NAM implementation and broader human-relevant technology strategy
jobs.immediate_action_now: Treat this as a high-value stretch role. Read the full experience requirement carefully before investing in a full application; if the management threshold is flexible, contact the hiring unit because the scientific match is unusually strong.

jobs.title: Post Doc Fellow, Department of Biomedical Engineering
jobs.company_info: The University of Cincinnati is a major public research university with a biomedical engineering department and a large regional biomedical ecosystem. The posting is department-level, so the precise laboratory and project fit need to be verified before treating it as a serious application.

salary.note: Salary was not surfaced in the current listing excerpt.

jobs.job_description: A biomedical engineering postdoctoral position at the University of Cincinnati. The listing excerpt does not identify enough project-specific detail to assume organ-on-chip relevance, so this should be screened by laboratory and mentor before applying.
key_must_have_requirements: PhD or equivalent doctoral training appropriate for biomedical engineering research
Ability to conduct independent research under faculty mentorship
Strong publication, experimental, and scientific communication skills
preferred_requirements: Direct alignment with the hiring laboratory's technical focus
jobs.why_good_match: The candidate's background is genuinely biomedical-engineering-shaped rather than only biological: organ-on-chip development, microfabrication, CFD, wet lab, and bioinformatics all create a broad platform for an interdisciplinary BME postdoc. The role becomes high-fit only if the specific mentor works in microphysiological systems, tissue engineering, microfluidics, biomaterials, or computational/experimental integration.
specific_experience_to_highlight: Soft lithography, porous PDMS membrane fabrication, and 3D-printing-assisted prototyping
Patient-derived organoids and advanced cell culture
gaps_or_risks: The posting is too broad to establish PI-level scientific fit from the listing alone
A generic postdoc is not automatically better than a targeted industry role or a highly aligned academic lab
Do not apply until the mentor, publication expectations, funding duration, and project ownership are clear
resume_tailoring: Use a balanced engineering-plus-biology CV rather than a disease-specific CV
Show technical breadth but organize it around one coherent theme: building and interrogating human-relevant engineered tissue systems
Include first-author engineering work and current disease-model manuscripts prominently
jobs.immediate_action_now: Identify the PI and project behind the posting first. Apply only if the lab materially advances the candidate toward independent organ-chip/NAM research rather than simply extending the PhD without adding a new capability.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor - Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine Institute
jobs.company: NYU Grossman School of Medicine / NYU Langone Health
jobs.company_info: NYU Grossman School of Medicine and its Regenerative Medicine Institute are recruiting tenure-track faculty at the Assistant/Associate Professor level in cell biology and regenerative medicine.

salary.note: Salary was not surfaced in the current listing excerpt.

jobs.job_description: Tenure-track recruitment in cell biology and regenerative medicine. This is not a near-term default application for a graduating PhD, but it is relevant as a benchmark for the kind of independent research profile the candidate could target after a productive postdoctoral period.
key_must_have_requirements: Strong record of original research and publication
Potential to establish an independent, externally funded research program
Research vision aligned with cell biology and regenerative medicine
preferred_requirements: Evidence of grant potential and collaborative fit
jobs.why_good_match: The candidate already has the seed of a distinctive independent niche: patient-derived organoids and microbiome integrated with stretchable organ-on-chip systems, bioinformatics, CFD, and microfabrication. The current gap is career stage rather than conceptual fit. A future faculty application could be unusually differentiated if the postdoc adds stronger independence, grant ownership, and a second biological system or translational application.
specific_experience_to_highlight: Integrated experimental biology + CFD + bioinformatics research identity
gaps_or_risks: Likely premature for an immediate faculty application without postdoctoral independence
Needs a clearly articulated independent research program distinct from the PhD advisor
Needs stronger evidence of grant readiness and sustained first/senior-author output
resume_tailoring: Use this posting as a faculty-readiness benchmark rather than a routine application
Start shaping a future research statement around a distinct platform question, not merely extending current gut-chip projects
Track which postdoctoral opportunities would add independence, funding ownership, and new biology rather than more of the same
jobs.immediate_action_now: Do not prioritize this over postdoc/staff-scientist roles unless the search explicitly welcomes unusually early applicants. Use it to reverse-engineer what the next 2–4 years need to produce for a competitive faculty launch.

briefings.overall_takeaway: For academia, the best near-term targets are not generic postdocs. Prioritize positions that add either scientific independence, a new capability, or direct ownership of human-relevant model platforms. An academic move should make the future PI story clearer, not simply extend the PhD by another title.
